items.title: Section: The Most Supreme Aspiration Towards the Three Jewels, and the Restraining Aspiration Delighting in the Precepts

items.zh: 謂諸菩薩，於佛法僧最上真實起勝意樂，是名菩薩最上意樂。又諸菩薩，於所受持淨戒律儀起勝意樂，是名菩薩遮止意樂。
items.en:
This means that bodhisattvas give rise to excellent aspiration towards the Buddha, the teaching, and the community as supreme and genuinely real. This is called a bodhisattva's most supreme aspiration.
Commentary: Regarding "towards the Buddha, the teaching, and the community as supreme and genuinely real" — the genuine qualities of the Buddha, the teaching, and the community eclipse every worldly and non-Buddhist alternative; this is why they are called supreme.
Furthermore, bodhisattvas give rise to excellent aspiration towards the pure precept-discipline they have received and uphold. This is called a bodhisattva's restraining aspiration.

items.title: Section: Delight in the Remaining Perfections, in Genuine Reality, and in the Buddhas' Own Inconceivable Power

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，於所修證施、忍、精進、靜慮、般若起勝意樂，是名菩薩波羅蜜多意樂。又諸菩薩，於法無我、補特伽羅無我、甚深勝義諸法真如起勝意樂，是名菩薩真實義意樂。又諸菩薩，於佛菩薩不可思議神通威力、或俱生威力起勝意樂，是名菩薩威力意樂。
items.en:
Furthermore, bodhisattvas give rise to excellent aspiration towards the cultivation and realisation of giving, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom. This is called a bodhisattva's aspiration of the perfections.
Furthermore, bodhisattvas give rise to excellent aspiration towards the selflessness of phenomena, the selflessness of the person, and the profound, ultimate suchness of all phenomena. This is called a bodhisattva's aspiration of genuine reality.
Furthermore, bodhisattvas give rise to excellent aspiration towards the buddhas' and bodhisattvas' own inconceivable supernormal power, and towards their innate power. This is called a bodhisattva's aspiration of power.

items.title: Section: The Wish to Give Wholesome Teaching, the Wish to Relieve Suffering, and Freedom From Attachment to Either — Three More Aspirations

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，於諸有情欲以善法而授與之，是名菩薩利益意樂。又諸菩薩、於諸有情，欲以饒益而授與之，是名菩薩安樂意樂。又諸菩薩，即於如是諸有情所無愛染心，又於當來可愛異熟其心無繫，是名菩薩解脫意樂。
items.en:
Furthermore, bodhisattvas wish to bestow wholesome teaching upon sentient beings. This is called a bodhisattva's aspiration of benefit.
Furthermore, bodhisattvas wish to bestow genuine relief upon sentient beings. This is called a bodhisattva's aspiration of ease.
Furthermore, bodhisattvas, towards these very same sentient beings, hold no attached, craving mind, and, towards whatever pleasant future karmic result might follow, their mind remains unbound. This is called a bodhisattva's aspiration of liberation.
Commentary: Regarding "towards these very same sentient beings, hold no attached, craving mind" — this means that the wish to give beings benefit and ease does not arise from any attachment or craving in the mind.

items.title: Section: Firm Resolve Towards Awakening, and Undistorted Wisdom Regarding the Actual Means of Helping Beings and Attaining It

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，於其無上正等菩提，其心專注，曾無變易，是名菩薩堅固意樂。又諸菩薩，於諸有情饒益方便，於大菩提趣證方便，無顛倒智俱行勝解，是名菩薩無虛妄意樂。
items.en:
Furthermore, bodhisattvas, towards unsurpassed, correct, complete awakening, hold a mind single-mindedly focused, never once wavering. This is called a bodhisattva's firm aspiration.
Furthermore, bodhisattvas hold undistorted wisdom joined with resolute understanding regarding the means of benefiting sentient beings, and regarding the means of approaching and realising great awakening. This is called a bodhisattva's undistorted aspiration.

items.title: Section: Impure, Pure, and Utterly Pure Aspiration — Tracking the Gradual Severing of the Two Obscurations Across the Grounds

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，勝解行地所有一切增上意樂，是名菩薩不清淨意樂。又諸菩薩，從淨勝意樂地乃至決定行地所有一切增上意樂，是名菩薩清淨意樂。又諸菩薩，到究竟地所有一切增上意樂，是名菩薩善清淨意樂。
items.en:
Furthermore, every excellent aspiration belonging to bodhisattvas at the stage of resolute practice is called a bodhisattva's impure aspiration.
Furthermore, every excellent aspiration belonging to bodhisattvas from the ground of pure, excellent aspiration through the ground of certain conduct is called a bodhisattva's pure aspiration.
Furthermore, every excellent aspiration belonging to bodhisattvas who have reached the ultimate ground is called a bodhisattva's utterly pure aspiration.

items.title: Section: The Aspiration Still to Be Tamed, and the Innate Aspiration That Has Become Second Nature — Closing All Fifteen Kinds and Opening the Ten Resulting Accomplishments

items.zh: 又諸菩薩不清淨意樂，是則名為應調伏意樂，由此意樂應思擇故。又諸菩薩清淨意樂、善清淨意樂，是則名為俱生意樂，由此意樂性成就故，於所依中善安立故。如是菩薩十五妙善增上意樂，隨一切地，以要言之，能作十事。
items.en:
Furthermore, a bodhisattva's impure aspiration is thereby called the aspiration for what is to be tamed, because this aspiration is precisely what must be discerned and examined.
Furthermore, a bodhisattva's pure aspiration and utterly pure aspiration are thereby called the innate aspiration, because this aspiration has become one's own nature, and because it is genuinely well-established within its own basis.
Commentary: Regarding "because this aspiration has become one's own nature" and the like — arising not through deliberate reflection but as a habituated nature is called becoming one's own nature. What is habituated nature? It means that, through repeated habituation in wholesome teachings, wholesome qualities accumulate within one's own supporting, ripening consciousness, remaining firm, unforgotten, and brought to their own ultimate completion — it is precisely by this meaning that it is called genuinely well-established.
These fifteen wondrous, excellent kinds of excellent aspiration a bodhisattva holds, spanning every stage, in brief, accomplish ten undertakings.

items.title: Section: Ten Accomplishments Open — Supreme Offering to the Three Jewels, and Precept-Keeping Even When Life Itself Is Threatened

items.zh: 何等為十？謂諸菩薩最上意樂，能於三寶修一切種最勝供養，普於一切菩提資糧為最第一。又諸菩薩遮止意樂，能於所受淨戒律儀，命難因緣，亦不故思犯於所犯；設有所犯，疾疾悔除。
items.en:
What are these ten? Through a bodhisattva's most supreme aspiration, one is able to make every kind of most excellent offering to the three jewels, foremost among all provisions gathered towards awakening.
Furthermore, through a bodhisattva's restraining aspiration, one is able, even under threat to one's own life, never to deliberately violate the pure precept-discipline received; should any violation occur regardless, one swiftly and thoroughly confesses and removes it.

items.title: Section: Tireless Practice of the Perfections, and Remaining in Birth-and-Death Without Taint, Never Rushing Into Premature Nirvana

items.zh: 又諸菩薩波羅蜜多意樂，能於善法常勤修習無放逸住，常住最勝無放逸住。又諸菩薩真實義意樂，能為有情以無染心流轉生死，不捨涅槃增上意樂。
items.en:
Furthermore, through a bodhisattva's aspiration of the perfections, one is able to diligently cultivate wholesome teachings continuously, dwelling free of heedlessness, abiding constantly in the most excellent freedom from heedlessness.
Furthermore, through a bodhisattva's aspiration of genuine reality, one is able, for the sake of sentient beings, to circulate through birth-and-death with an untainted mind, holding the excellent aspiration never to enter nirvana prematurely.
Commentary: Regarding "circulate through birth-and-death with an untainted mind" and the like — because bodhisattvas genuinely, correctly know birth-and-death as it truly is, they circulate through it with an untainted mind. Because they do not hold excessive longing for nirvana, they do not hasten to enter final nirvana. This meaning is as explained in the Chapter on Genuine Reality.

items.title: Section: Tasting the Pure, Wondrous Flavour of the Teaching Through the Aspiration of Power — Never Satisfied With Mere Hearing and Reflecting Alone

items.zh: 又諸菩薩威力意樂，能於聖教覺受淳淨上妙法味。復能於修起堅固想，欣樂多住，不唯聞思便生喜足。
items.en:
Furthermore, through a bodhisattva's aspiration of power, one is able to genuinely taste, within the noble teaching, its own pure, wondrous flavour.
Commentary: Regarding "genuinely taste, within the noble teaching, its own pure, wondrous flavour" — the Stage of Meditative Equipoise explains: there are four correct dharmas that sustain the true teaching. What are these four? First, seclusion; second, cultivation; third, the fruit of cultivation; fourth, freedom from any contention within the noble teaching. And so on, as explained at length. The "noble teaching" mentioned here should be understood according to that explanation. Through cultivating calm-abiding and insight, genuinely penetrating the noble teaching's own meaning, free of any contradiction with it, is what is called genuinely tasting this pure, wondrous flavour.
One is further able to give rise to firm resolve regarding actual cultivation, delighting in sustained dwelling within it, not remaining satisfied with mere hearing and reflecting alone.
Commentary: Regarding "give rise to firm resolve regarding actual cultivation, delighting in sustained dwelling" — this means reflecting as follows: cultivating a concentrated mind, attaining mastery over concentration, one is able to correctly counter every contaminated, defiling phenomenon, never again overpowered by such contaminated, defiling phenomena. This is called giving rise to firm resolve regarding cultivation, and it is precisely because of this that one delights in sustained dwelling within cultivation.

items.title: Section: Tireless Benefiting of Beings, Blazing Diligence, and Never Settling for Partial Attainment

items.zh: 又諸菩薩利益意樂、安樂意樂、解脫意樂，能於一切饒益有情所作事業精勤修習，雖常修習而無厭倦。又諸菩薩堅固意樂，能於種種熾然精進、廣大精進，發起安住無緩加行、無斷加行。又諸菩薩無虛妄意樂，能於所引彼彼善法速證通慧，不於少分下劣薄弱差別證中而生喜足。
items.en:
Furthermore, through a bodhisattva's aspiration of benefit, aspiration of ease, and aspiration of liberation together, one is able to diligently cultivate every undertaking that benefits sentient beings, and though constantly cultivating it, never grow weary.
Furthermore, through a bodhisattva's firm aspiration, one is able to give rise to every kind of blazing, vast diligence, sustaining effort that neither slackens nor breaks off.
Furthermore, through a bodhisattva's undistorted aspiration, one is able to swiftly realise supernormal knowledge and ultimate wisdom with respect to whatever wholesome teachings have been taken up, never growing satisfied with some small, inferior, or weak degree of attainment.

items.title: Section: The Aspiration Still to Be Tamed Draws Forth the Innate Aspiration, Which in Turn Swiftly Completes Awakening Itself — Closing the Ten Accomplishments

items.zh: 又諸菩薩應調伏意樂，能引俱生意樂。又諸菩薩俱生意樂，能於無上正等菩提速疾趣證；能與天人作諸義利利益安樂。
items.en:
Furthermore, through a bodhisattva's aspiration for what is to be tamed, one is able to draw forth the innate aspiration.
Furthermore, through a bodhisattva's innate aspiration, one is able to swiftly approach and realise unsurpassed, correct, complete awakening, and to bring gods and humans genuine welfare, benefit, and ease.

items.title: Section: Three Aspirations Left Unrepeated, All Fifteen Comprehensively Cover Everything the Buddha Teaches — Chapter Three Closes in Full

items.zh: 應調伏意樂即不清淨意樂，俱生意樂即清淨意樂、善清淨意樂，故不別說。世尊所有為諸菩薩，於彼彼處種種宣說、施設、開示增上意樂，當知一切即此十五意樂所攝，是故過去、未來、現在妙善意樂諸菩薩眾，於其無上正等菩提曾當現證，一切皆由如是所說十五意樂。除此無有若過若增。如是菩薩十五意樂，能得最大菩提果利，是故菩薩依此意樂，速證無上正等菩提。
items.en:
The aspiration for what is to be tamed is itself the impure aspiration; the innate aspiration is itself the pure aspiration and the utterly pure aspiration. This is why they are not separately explained again here.
Whatever the world-honoured one has, in this place or that, variously taught, established, and disclosed to bodhisattvas regarding excellent aspiration, one should understand, is entirely comprised within these fifteen kinds of excellent aspiration. This is why every bodhisattva of the past, future, and present who holds this wondrous, excellent aspiration, and who has already realised, will realise, or presently realises unsurpassed, correct, complete awakening, does so entirely through these fifteen kinds of excellent aspiration already explained. Beyond these, there is nothing to be added and nothing lacking.
Since these fifteen kinds of excellent aspiration a bodhisattva holds bring the very greatest benefit and fruit of awakening, bodhisattvas who rely on this aspiration swiftly realise unsurpassed, correct, complete awakening.

blocks.text: Fifteen kinds of excellent aspiration, from delight in the Three Jewels to aspiration so habitual it has become one's nature, and ten accomplishments that follow from them.

Master Cháng Bǎi: pure precepts govern the mind; discipline is the bodily and verbal conduct that appears in response to objects. Venerable Miào Jìng: break precepts carelessly and concentration is hard.
"Towards the selflessness of phenomena, of persons, and the profound ultimate suchness." Master Cháng Bǎi: the deeper one's understanding, the greater the joy.
Venerable Miào Jìng: the mind focused on ultimate truth; no retreating from the great to the small.

"From the ground of pure aspiration through the ground of certain conduct": Venerable Miào Jìng, the first ground to the ninth. Before turning from ordinary to noble, the seeds of both obscurations remain uncut, so the aspiration is "impure".
Master Cháng Bǎi: through habituation these qualities become part of one's character, "become one's nature"; without deliberate choosing, the aspiration for the perfections arises spontaneously.

"Even under threat to life, never deliberately violating; should a breach occur, swiftly confessing it." Master Cháng Bǎi: the Buddha spoke of two heroes: one who does no wrong, and one who confesses after doing it.

subs.head: Neither fearing nor rushing into nirvāṇa

blocks.text: Master Cháng Bǎi: they neither fear nirvāṇa like ordinary beings nor delight in it like śrāvakas. Venerable Miào Jìng: in the contemplation of ultimate emptiness there is nothing lovable or hateful, so the mind stays pure in saṃsāra.
Master Cháng Bǎi: one must advance "even from the top of a hundred-foot pole".
Venerable Miào Jìng: beings of the three lower realms find it hard to accomplish the noble paths; humans and gods find it easier, so only gods and humans are named.
"Two heroes": one who does no wrong, and one who confesses. Most of us will be the second kind, and the Buddha calls that heroic too.

quiz.q: "Restraining aspiration" concerns pure precepts and discipline. How do the lectures distinguish 淨戒 and 律儀?
options: both: pure precepts are of the mind, discipline is its outward bodily-verbal expression; Miào Jìng adds that careless breaches make concentration hard
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: pure precepts govern the mind; discipline is the bodily and verbal conduct that appears in response to objects. Venerable Miào Jìng: pure precepts are spoken of the mind, discipline its outward expression; break precepts carelessly and concentration is hard.

quiz.q: "Aspiration of genuine reality" is aspiration towards what?
options: the selflessness of phenomena and of persons, the profound ultimate suchness
quiz.why: "Towards the selflessness of phenomena, of persons, and the profound ultimate suchness." Master Cháng Bǎi: the deeper one's understanding, the greater the joy.

quiz.q: On "firm aspiration," how does Venerable Miào Jìng explain "single-minded focus"?
options: focused on ultimate truth — suchness is supreme awakening; no retreat to the lesser vehicle
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: the mind focused on ultimate truth — the suchness of phenomena is supreme awakening; no retreating from the great to the small.

options: from the ground of pure aspiration through the ground of certain conduct
quiz.why: "From the ground of pure aspiration through the ground of certain conduct." Venerable Miào Jìng: the ground of pure aspiration is the first ground, where afflictions begin to be cut; the ground of certain conduct is the ninth.

quiz.q: Why is aspiration at the stage of resolute practice "impure"? What does Master Cháng Bǎi say?
options: before turning ordinary to noble, the seeds of both obscurations are not yet cut
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: before turning from ordinary to noble, the seeds of afflictive and cognitive obscuration remain uncut. Venerable Miào Jìng: afflictions not yet cut — seeds remain, so the aspiration is impure.

quiz.q: "Innate aspiration — because it has become one's nature." How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain this?
options: fine qualities, through habituation, become character — part of one's very life
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: these fine qualities, through habituation, are internalised into character, part of one's life — "become one's nature"; without deliberate choosing, the aspiration of the perfections arises spontaneously.

quiz.q: What does restraining aspiration accomplish, even under threat to life?
options: even under threat to life, never deliberately violating; any breach swiftly confessed
quiz.why: "Even under threat to life, never deliberately violating; should a breach occur, swiftly confessing it." Venerable Miào Jìng: better to die than not keep the precepts pure. Master Cháng Bǎi: the Buddha spoke of two heroes — one who does no wrong, one who confesses after doing it.

quiz.q: Aspiration of genuine reality lets bodhisattvas circulate in saṃsāra untainted, not entering nirvāṇa. What attitude towards nirvāṇa do the lectures describe?
options: Cháng Bǎi: neither fearing nirvāṇa like ordinary people nor craving it like śrāvakas; Miào Jìng: in ultimate emptiness nothing is lovable or hateful — the mind stays pure in saṃsāra, unlike the arhat's swift nirvāṇa
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: they neither fear nirvāṇa like ordinary beings nor delight in it like śrāvakas. Venerable Miào Jìng: in the contemplation of ultimate emptiness there's nothing lovable or hateful, so the mind stays pure in saṃsāra — unlike arhats who swiftly enter nirvāṇa.

quiz.q: Undistorted aspiration means "never settling for partial attainment." What does Master Cháng Bǎi say?
options: knowing practice isn't complete, never satisfied with little — step forward from the top of a hundred-foot pole
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: understanding that one's practice isn't yet complete, never content with little — one must advance even from the top of a hundred-foot pole.

quiz.q: Innate aspiration "brings benefit to gods and humans." Why only gods and humans, according to Venerable Miào Jìng?
options: beings of the three lower realms find the noble path hard; humans and gods find it easier
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: beings of the three lower realms find it hard to accomplish the three vehicles' noble paths; humans and gods find it easier — so only gods and humans are named.
